title: Operator CLI: trigger provisioning run + safe stage re-run (with dry-run)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
We’re automating Dedicated pool bring-up end-to-end (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed). Operators still need a reliable, explicit entrypoint to (a) start a provisioning run and (b) re-run individual stages safely when the pipeline hits transient failures.

This ticket adds operator-facing CLI commands that call the control plane provisioning APIs. It must be safe-by-default, auditable, and support a dry-run mode for change review / coordination.

Goals
- Provide a supported operator CLI to:
  1) Trigger a provisioning run for an existing pool (new pool request or expansion).
  2) Re-run a specific stage for an existing provisioning run (e.g., re-run Validating only).
- Include a dry-run mode that prints the actions that would be taken (including derived inputs) without making changes.
- Make it hard to do the wrong thing:
  - require explicit confirmation for mutating operations
  - validate stage transitions locally where possible
  - surface clear status + links (run status, dashboards, logs)
- Ensure auditability: every invocation should have an operator identity, reason (optional but encouraged), and correlation ID.

Non-goals
- Building a full UI for provisioning.
- Replacing the Slack bot status updates.
- Implementing the underlying state machine, readiness gates, or Terraform orchestration logic (owned by separate tickets).

User stories
- As Fleet Ops, I can start a provisioning run for pool=ded-foo in us-east so I don’t need to hit internal APIs manually.
- As SRE, I can re-run the validation stage after a transient DNS failure without re-imaging nodes.
- As oncall, I can run a dry-run during an incident to sanity-check inputs and expected steps before touching prod.

Proposed CLI surface area
Command group: rw fleet provision

1) Trigger a run
- rw fleet provision run --pool <pool_id> [--reason "..."] [--dry-run] [--wait] [--timeout 30m] [--staging|--prod]
- Behavior:
  - dry-run: prints derived request payload, resolved control-plane endpoint, and validation results (schema checks, stage eligibility) but does not submit.
  - non-dry-run: submits run request, prints run_id + correlation_id.
  - --wait tails run status until Ready/Failed/Canceled or timeout.

2) Re-run a stage
- rw fleet provision rerun-stage --run <run_id> --stage <Provisioning|Imaging|Bootstrapping|Validating|PerfCanary> [--reason "..."] [--dry-run] [--wait]
- Safety rules:
  - Only allow rerun when run state is Failed or operator-paused (or explicitly allow rerun from Validating if stage is terminal but run not marked Ready).
  - Disallow rerun of prior stages if a later stage has already completed successfully unless --force (admin-only) and logged.
  - If rerun-stage is invoked with --dry-run, print what would be re-used vs re-created (e.g., cached artifacts, cluster ID, terraform outputs).

3) Inspect run status (quality-of-life)
- rw fleet provision status --run <run_id>
- rw fleet provision status --pool <pool_id> --latest

Output requirements
- Human-friendly by default (table-ish summary) and machine-friendly with --json.
- Always print:
  - environment (staging/prod)
  - pool_id
  - run_id
  - current_state
  - last_transition_at
  - correlation_id
  - links: control plane run page, readiness dashboard filtered to pool/run

AuthZ / Security
- CLI uses Redwood SSO token (same mechanism as existing operator tools) and calls control plane APIs.
- Mutating commands require:
  - operator membership in “fleet-operators” (or “sre-oncall”) group
  - explicit interactive confirmation unless --yes is provided
- Add optional --reason, encourage usage; include in audit log entry.

Telemetry
- Emit structured log on invocation (client-side) including command, env, pool/run, dry_run flag, and correlation_id.
- Server-side audit log is the source of truth; CLI should print the audit event ID returned by the API if available.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] CLI can trigger provisioning run for a pool in staging.
- [x] CLI can rerun Validating stage for a failed run without starting a new run.
- [x] dry-run prints derived payload + eligibility checks and makes no API calls that mutate state.
- [x] Output includes run_id, correlation_id, and dashboard link.
- [x] Commands require confirmation (or --yes) for non-dry-run.
- [x] RBAC is enforced (403 surfaced clearly).
- [x] Adds basic docs/help text + examples.

Open questions
- Do we want --force for stage rerun (admin-only) in v1, or defer until we have more operational experience?
- Do we require --reason for prod mutations? (Currently optional; we can make it required later once operators are used to it.)

References
- Project overview: Confluence “Provision-to-ready automation overview”
- Control plane API endpoint work: see provisioning API PR
- Operator feedback thread: oncall asked for clearer error classification and a safe rerun path

comments: 2025-02-19 (Vanessa Ortiz): Adding this as a blocking operator-experience item for the pilot. We can’t rely on curl + bespoke scripts during staging/prod rollout. Please make sure the CLI prints the dashboard link with pool_id/run_id filters, and requires confirmation for prod.

2025-02-21 (Gabe Wilson): Drafted command structure: `rw fleet provision run` + `rw fleet provision rerun-stage`. Implementing `--dry-run` to build request payload and run local validation only (no POST). For safety I’m adding `--yes` required for non-interactive runs in CI.

2025-02-24 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure rerun-stage refuses to rerun Imaging/Bootstrapping if Validating already passed and Ready was set. We had a near-miss last quarter where an operator re-imaged nodes under load. Even if the API blocks this, the CLI should be defensive and print next steps (pause/resume or start a new run).

2025-02-26 (Gabe Wilson): Implemented local guardrails: stage rerun checks current state via GET before submitting. Added `--wait` which polls every 10s and prints stage transitions. Also printing correlation_id and “Run details” URL from the API response.

2025-03-03 (Benji Okafor): CLI output should clearly show whether config validation passed/failed and link to the validation error docs/runbook section. Even if validation is a server-side stage, the operator needs an actionable message.

2025-03-06 (Gabe Wilson): Addressed: on failure, CLI prints top-level error category + runbook link. Added `--json` output for bot/automation consumption. Dry-run now prints resolved env endpoint + derived inputs (pool_id, requested SKU/region from control plane pool record) and explicitly states “NO CHANGES APPLIED”.

2025-03-10 (Connor O'Brien): For release: please gate the new CLI subcommands behind the same feature flag as the provisioning pipeline in staging. We don’t want operators accidentally calling the new endpoints in prod until rollout approval.

2025-03-14 (Vanessa Ortiz): Marking done after staging pilot. CLI was used during the staging checklist and helped rerun Validating after transient DNS flake without restarting the whole workflow. Follow-up: consider requiring --reason for prod mutations once we have a couple of weeks of usage.
